speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MediShield Life, our national health insurance scheme, was launched in 2015 and is an integral part of Singapore's "S+3Ms" healthcare financing framework, comprising subsidies, MediShield Life, MediSave and MediFund.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MediShield Life protects all Singaporeans against large healthcare bills for life, regardless of pre-existing health conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This ensures that no Singaporean is denied appropriate healthcare due to an inability to pay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The MediShield Life Scheme Act 2015, or the Act, was enacted in 2015 to support the establishment, governance and administration of MediShield Life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Act has not been amended since it was passed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Since then, two key developments have taken place, which warrant amendments to the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: First, the landscape for healthcare delivery has evolved since MediShield Life's launch in 2015.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The centre of gravity for healthcare delivery has been shifting to the outpatient, community and home settings, because not all patients require care in a hospital for their treatment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: With this shift, more patients can benefit from easier access to necessary care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: To support this, MediShield Life coverage has been gradually expanded to more types of treatments beyond the acute inpatient setting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, in 2020, we expanded MediShield Life to cover inpatient palliative care within community hospitals and inpatient hospices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We are continuing our efforts to do more to support care outside of the acute inpatient setting, in the community and at home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: One example is the Home Ventilation and Respiratory Support Service (HVRSS), which provides mechanical-assisted ventilation to persons with breathing insufficiency, in the comfort of their homes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We need to amend the Act to allow MediShield Life to cover the increasing number of treatments that are now being delivered beyond the hospital setting as well as new care models that may emerge in the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Second, over the last nine years since its launch, the Government has gained more experience in administering MediShield Life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We have identified issues that have limited our ability to administer it effectively and efficiently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: A key area to be covered in this regard is premium recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: When MediShield Life was made universal in 2015, it became mandatory for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents to pay their premiums and contribute to the national risk pool.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This also means that we must recover premiums from those who are able to but evade making payments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Having had nine years of experience administering this, we have identified areas where the Act needs to be strengthened to better support premium recovery and improve scheme administration.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Our first objective is to support the expansion of MediShield Life coverage to new models of care received outside the physical premises of healthcare providers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: First, we will amend the Act to redefine where treatments or services can be received.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This means that the scheme will be able to cover care that is received entirely outside the premises of a medical institution and provides flexibility to cover newer care models that may develop in future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Second, we will set out a clearer and more robust governance framework that allows scoped approvals, and suspensions and revocations of such approvals, of medical institutions in respect of approved medical treatment or services they provide under MediShield Life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Under the framework, the Minister for Health can approve providers to be approved medical institutions in respect of specific approved medical treatment or services and/or specific delivery modes for the purposes of MediShield Life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Additionally, where a "medical institution" has been granted more than one licence under the Healthcare Services Act 2020 to provide "licensable healthcare services", the Minister has the prerogative to approve all, or only one or some of such licensable healthcare services provided by the approved medical institution for the purposes of MediShield Life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will also introduce provisions to enable the Minister to impose conditions of approval and to suspend or revoke the approvals given.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: To support the framework, clause 2(c) of the Bill amends section 2(1) by introducing a new concept of "claimable medical treatment or services".

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This ensures that the scheme only covers medical treatments or services provided by approved medical institutions according to the scope of their approval.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Under the new amendments, the Minister is also empowered to grant approvals to medical institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Taken together, the amendments will allow MediShield Life to be responsive to emerging models of care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: It will also enable the Act to be more targeted in its approvals, and suspension and revocation of the approval of providers and their claimable medical treatment or services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This will strengthen the accountability of approved medical institutions and ensure compliance with the claim guidelines for MediShield Life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MediShield Life is a universal scheme which relies on collective responsibility through risk-pooling, to provide all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents peace of mind in affording large, unexpected healthcare bills throughout their lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: All policyholders must play their part by paying their premiums.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This ensures that MediShield Life can continue to meet its obligations and support those of us who fall ill and need to make a claim.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: At the same time, we recognise the need to keep premiums affordable, especially for vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This is why the Government provides strong support in the form of premium subsidies for lower- and middle-income households, Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation subsidies, and additional MediSave top-ups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We also have a comprehensive set of measures to facilitate the payment of premiums.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, for those who have missed premium payment due to insufficient MediSave balances, we remind them to top up MediSave and facilitate the process for immediate family members to take over premium payment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For those who need further help with their premiums even after subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support, we will assess their eligibility for Additional Premium Support (APS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, there are some individuals who do not pay their premiums despite these measures and become defaulters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In such cases, premium recovery and enforcement is needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Any owed premiums that cannot be recovered will affect the MediShield Life Fund's sustainability and ultimately, affect MediShield Life's ability to meet its claims.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: If left unrecovered, these debts will have to be shouldered by other policyholders in the form of higher premiums.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: A key enabler of this premium recovery process is the service of a demand note.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Today, a demand note needs to be served before recovery measures, such as the appointment of an agent to recover outstanding premiums, and the imposition of interest and penalties for late payments can commence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The note may be served by the prescribed recovery bodies under the Act – the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board and the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: At present, demand notes are only deemed served if sent by registered post to a person's residential address provided in accordance with section 31 of the Act or any correspondence address provided by the person under certain prescribed circumstances.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This is pursuant to regulations made under the limited scope provided by section 34(2)(k) of the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, this has impeded the recovery of outstanding premiums, such as in cases where no valid address information on the defaulter is available or service at an overseas address is required.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Clause 10 of the Bill inserts the new sections 33A and 33B.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The new sections provide how demand notes and other documents permitted or required by or under the Act to be served may be effectively served.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, a demand note may be served by sending it to an email address of a person where there is deemed consent to such service in accordance with the new section 33B(3)(b).

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Minister is also empowered to make regulations to allow a demand note to be served via an existing electronic service such as CPF Board's "my cpf" portal or IRAS' "myTax Portal" by applying the requirements set out in existing laws regarding these electronic services to the service of demand notes by CPF Board or IRAS respectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This facilitates recovery bodies in their recovery efforts, especially in relation to individuals on whom they were previously unable to serve demand notes and documents by registered post.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: While we have a strong set of recovery measures to ensure the sustainability of the scheme, we should take a calibrated approach based on the means of defaulters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, some defaulters may come from lower-income households with complex circumstances.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We should be more empathetic towards such groups of people and provide them a longer time to pay their outstanding premiums.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: On the other hand, premium recovery should proceed along the normal timelines for those with more means to pay their outstanding premiums, such as individuals from higher-income households.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: First, we will specify MediShield Life premiums in a manner that is more accessible, such as on MOH's website, instead of legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Currently, MediShield Life premiums must be prescribed in regulations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This mirrors the practice adopted for CareShield Life, our national long-term care insurance scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Second, we will make clear the date when a person is taken to attain a particular age for the purposes of calculating their MediShield Life premiums.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This is achieved through the amendment to section 2(4) of the Act by clause 2(f).

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For most Singaporeans, their age is taken to be on their birth anniversary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, there is a small group of individuals whose birth date and/or month cannot be ascertained.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Currently, our practice is to take their birth date to be on the first day of the month in which the individual was born, if their birth date cannot be ascertained; and their birth month to be in January, if their birth month cannot be ascertained.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This is not currently set out in legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The proposed amendment to section 2(4) will clarify this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: There is another group of individuals who are born on a leap day.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For them, MediShield Life starts on 29 February in the year they are born and in subsequent years, their birth anniversary is taken to be on 1 March.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This mirrors the approach taken by CareShield Life today and ensures consistency across our schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This amendment will not impact these individuals' MediShield Life cover or premiums, as there will not be any breaks in their coverage and premiums continue to be calculated based on their age over the insurance period.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Lastly, we will expand the scope of offences arising out of false or misleading information provided under the Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Today, section 19 makes it an offence where a person knowingly provides material information which is false or misleading and knowing that the information will be included in a health declaration, means declaration or claim application.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The amendments by clause 6 to section 19 provide for this.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The amendments will enable us to take a stricter stance against such offenders and ensure the proper payment of claims as well as the disbursement of grants and subsidies, to protect the interest of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Act serves as the fundamental legislative framework that enables the implementation and operation of MediShield Life, an important component of our S+3Ms healthcare financing framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This Bill ensures that coverage of MediShield Life keeps pace with changes to our healthcare landscape whilst allowing the Government to more effectively and efficiently administer the scheme.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: With an ageing population and people living longer, healthcare needs and costs are rising.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I do note that the Minister of State in her speech did share about the fact that these new treatments are only for approved medical institutions and only for the approved scope of these medical institutions.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: If this is the case, I think it will be also very important that this is clearly communicated to patients when they do seek these treatments, so that we will not have a situation of the assumption that it will be covered and then we have a situation where they are not covered, they are not eligible.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: With increasing healthcare cost, these proposed changes are welcomed as it will help patients manage large medical bills.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The increase in claims for existing outpatient treatments covered by MediShield Life and the inclusion of additional new patient treatments will hopefully encourage more appropriate and right-siting of care.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Currently, some patients do opt for inpatient care at hospitals for treatments that may not require hospitalisation as claims or coverage for these treatments are not covered for outpatient treatments or day surgeries, leading to unnecessary costs and wastage.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: When one is ill, being able to afford and have access to appropriate treatment is not only important for the well-being for persons who are ill but also gives peace of mind to the patient and their family members.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Thus, having appropriate and sufficient healthcare insurance to handle unexpected or sudden health situations that require surgery or major treatments and hospitalisation will help ensure affordability for all, for treatments and for large bills.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, while I support the proposed amendments, there are a few points I would like to speak on and seek clarification in my speech today and the focus is on how these amendments may impact the individual.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I know that the Bill is meant to handle the specific frameworks for the implementation of MediShield Life, but ultimately, MediShield Life touches lives and touches individuals so I would like to touch on these points.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, first, on higher deductibles and affordability; second, on more support and guidance on Integrated Shield Plans and decisions on Integrated Shield Plans; third, on pre and post-hospitalisation coverage; and fourth, premium subsidies and MediSave top-ups.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The increase in MediSave withdrawal limits will help patients pay for the increase in deductibles.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Deductibles are an important feature of MediShield Life to prevent overuse or overconsumption of healthcare spending and to ensure that coverage of MediShield Life is for specifically larger medical bills.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: If faced with such circumstances, what help can they seek?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: On pre- and post-hospitalisation coverage, in the consideration for expansion of coverage for MediShield Life to cover large medical bills, was consideration given to include pre and post-hospitalisation treatments prior to the need for inpatient services?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Maybe I should have asked this question of the Review Committee rather than of the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: But the reason why I am asking for this is because usually, most patients, prior to admission will require several consultations and scans or tests to be done to ascertain their condition and early-stage treatments which are usually outpatient.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: After discharge from hospitals, they may also require recovery treatments, and these can add up and sometimes cost more than a hospital stay.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I understand that there is always trade-offs and balances of what gets covered and premium affordability.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: But given the intent of MediShield Life to ensure affordability for larger medical treatments, can there be an option in MediShield Life for those who require coverage for pre and post-hospitalisation treatment to pay an additional premium for the coverage.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While there could be adverse selection and this will increase premium payable for those who do select the premium, it will be more affordable than having to make out-of-pocket payment for pre and post hospitalisation charges.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For some who have an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) that covers pre- and post-hospitalisation charges, the reason they have cited for having IPs to enable them to be able to get an earlier appointment to consult a specialist either at a public hospital or private hospital but usually they do it at the public hospital and the feedback is that as a non-subsidised patient, it is easier to get an earlier appointment to see a specialist at the public hospital and to have the appropriate tests and diagnosis.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, apart from coverage of medical expenses, on the other side is the capacity of specialist consultation and tests at public hospitals and this will need to also be balanced and reviewed.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I know this is again not part of the Bill, but at the end of the day, when you look at MediShield Life and you look at coverage, it is about treatment that is received and the institutions where they are received – and our public hospitals are held in very high regard for the quality of their services.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: With the increase in the claim limits and expansion of coverage and benefits of MediShield Life, will MOH consider providing more support and advice to Singaporeans on the appropriate coverage for healthcare insurance?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: And why I am saying this is because it was reported that about half of patients with IPs for private hospitals still end up using subsidised care at public hospitals.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, what it means is that they are paying for healthcare insurance that they do not even use.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This is costly and unnecessary expense and put financial strain especially for seniors as IP premiums cost a lot more.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While there is a lot of information on IP including cost comparisons, the fact is that so many are paying for what they do not use and that shows that more can be done to help Singaporeans make the right decisions on their healthcare insurance.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For some, the proposed amendments with the increase in claim limits, expansion of coverage and benefits could mean that MediShield Life may indeed give adequate coverage and the decision could be to give up their IPs which cost more as one ages.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: We do need however to understand that the decision for one to give up an IP needs to be considered carefully as eligibility to purchase coverage for IPs require one to be in good health and with no pre-existing conditions.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, if they give it up, they would problems getting back on.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: But the cost of IP really is quite high as one ages.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The proposed premium subsidies and MediSave top-ups are needed and will help the affordability of premiums and will cushion the impact of the increase for most Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This is not a bIanket approval that I am asking for but to be able to look at it on individuals that may need it and why I say this because we do have residents who cannot afford to own their own homes and they have on the goodwill of their relatives been able to stay with their relatives.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: And some of them live in residences that are valued higher than $25,000 and AV is what is used for means-testing and so some may require support for the premium but given their residential address, will not be eligible for the subsidies.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, I hope that MOH would look at this when appeals of such requests come up.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, in conclusion, Mr Deputy Speaker, while it is important that healthcare remains affordable and there is adequate medical coverage, paradoxically, our goal should be to stay healthy and not to have to use it often.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: In the spirit of Healthier SG, we should all do our part and lead healthy lifestyles.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: This would not only lower healthcare costs which is what we are talking about today but also improve the quality of life for individuals.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, I hope to see how this will work out as it goes, as it is implemented.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The proposed amendments are in line with the aspiration and principle to ensure that quality healthcare is accessible and affordable to all Singaporeans who need it.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Clause 11 amends section 34 of the Act, which grants the Minister broad powers to make regulations, including determining premium rates for different classes of insured persons.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This criterion could present a financial challenge for some low or no-income households, particularly retirees living in private property and are born in 1960 or later.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: These individuals may face rising medical bills yet do not qualify for premium subsidies due to the property they live in.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Many of these elderly Singaporeans are unlikely to downsize their homes, especially if they are currently suffering from serious illnesses.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The physical and emotional disruption of relocating during a vulnerable period is impractical and could worsen their health conditions.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This approach would allow the scheme to target subsidies more effectively towards those who genuinely lack cash flow for their healthcare needs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Clause 5 grants the Minister flexibility to set premium rates through prescribed means, possibly via online publications.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Although this change could streamline the process, I have some concerns about the stability and predictability of premium rates.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Policyholders, especially those with lower incomes, rely on consistent healthcare costs to plan their finances.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Frequent premium adjustments could challenge their ability to budget effectively.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Will the Government establish a regular schedule for premium adjustments, and if not, how much advance notice will policyholders receive to prepare for changes?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will provide policyholders with more transparency and predictability regarding their healthcare expenses.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Clause 4 grants the Minister discretion to approve medical institutions and the treatments they offer as eligible for MediShield Life claims.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Although this change may help manage costs, it could also limit access to necessary care if certain treatments or institutions do not receive approval.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Unapproved services might force policyholders to pay out-of-pocket, discouraging them from seeking essential treatment.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Could the Minister of State clarify if the criteria for approving medical services, and a complete list of approved services and institutions will be published regularly?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will help policyholders to make informed healthcare choices and avoid unexpected costs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Additionally, does this amendment allow the Minister to designate Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and other traditional medical practices as approved medical treatments in the future?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Many Singaporeans rely on TCM and other traditional practices for managing chronic conditions and maintaining overall health.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Clause 6 broadens the scope of offences related to false or misleading information in health declarations, means declarations or claims.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This amendment aims to deter fraud, but it may disproportionately impact elderly or less tech-savvy policyholders who may make honest mistakes in their submissions.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: What are the provisions for rectifying minor or first-time errors, especially for vulnerable groups?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Establishing a grace period or correction mechanism would prevent harsh penalties for honest mistakes, particularly for seniors unfamiliar with digital processes.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Clause 9 allows the Government to use means information to assess eligibility and support recovery actions for outstanding premiums.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Although this approach may ensure targeted resource allocation, it could place additional pressure on low-income policyholders.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Aggressive recovery actions, if based primarily on financial data, could create financial stress for households already struggling to meet healthcare costs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Will the Government provide safeguards like automatic premium loans or deferred payment options to protect financially vulnerable policyholders and help them maintain coverage without incurring penalties?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Will these policyholders lose coverage if they still fail to pay their premiums?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Clause 10 introduces electronic methods for serving official documents, including email, which may improve efficiency.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, policyholders who are less comfortable with digital platforms might miss important updates, potentially leading to unintended coverage lapses or penalties.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Does the Government offer additional communication methods, such as phone calls or in-person notifications, to ensure all policyholders receive and understand crucial information?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: For low-income households, I urge MOH to review the use of AV as a criterion for means testing, so that retirees and those with limited cash flow can receive subsidies based on their actual financial need.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I welcome the changes and support the latest MediShield Life Scheme (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Notwithstanding this, I would like to raise some clarifications relating to: one, the enhanced eligibility and coverage expansion for outpatient treatments and advanced therapeutics; two, deductible and co-insurance changes; three, premium adjustments; and four, emphasis on preventive care.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I welcome the increase in claim limits as it will ensure that Singaporeans can continue to receive adequate support during critical hospitalisation without compromising on the scheme's sustainability.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Additionally, the Bill has made amendments to include newly defined terms such as "approved medical institution", "claimable medical treatment or services" and "licensable healthcare service".

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With the expansion of outpatient coverage, patients will also have more access to convenient care options beyond the traditional hospital settings.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Similarly, I am supportive of the expanded coverage of high-cost treatments and high-cost drugs for blood conditions and conditions with childhood onset, that are clinically effective and cost-effective.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This will ensure that these medications remain accessible to those who need them, while keeping insurance premiums and overall bill costs affordable.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Nevertheless, given the newly recommended claim limits mentioned for high-cost treatments, I would like to ask how would MOH address concerns about the sustainability of covering such treatments in the long run?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have several clarifications to make regarding the expanded eligibility and the impact on service access.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to ask MOH what safeguards are in place to control cost increases resulting from a higher volume of outpatient claims to be expected?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Additionally, how does MOH plan to balance the inclusion of a wide range of outpatient services while preventing over-utilisation, which may drive up overall healthcare costs in the long term?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My concerns lie with the impact of increased deductibles on lower-income households, especially lower-income seniors who are staying alone, as well as those with frequent outpatient needs.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These families and individuals may not have sufficient MediSave to cover the deductibles and may end up having an increased out-of-pocket cashflow burden.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that MOH can consider additional support or a tiered deductible structure for such cases through some forms of means-testing of their household incomes.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This will help patients to worry less about their out-of-pocket payments if they have insufficient MediSave funds.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Additionally, I also hope that MOH can consider including Flexi-MediSave in the consideration of the deductibles that are currently calculated.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many residents of mine in Jalan Kayu, who have issues with their medical bills, spoke to me about the limits imposed on the Flexi-MediSave, increasing their out-of-pocket cash payments.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These are especially so, for those who have frequent Specialist Outpatient Clinic appointments for regular reviews of their medical conditions.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I do support this move to ensure large outpatient bills remain affordable for subsidised patients.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Nevertheless, I hope to understand how MOH will determine the tiered co-insurance.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What will be the specific threshold that will dictate that co-insurance percentage to be used for the outpatient bill and how is this threshold calculated by MOH?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would now like to focus on a key concern that impacts our residents the most – the adjustments of the MediShield Life premiums.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With the rise in policy claim limits and the expanded scope of coverage to include high-cost treatments, premium adjustments are an inevitable measure to maintain the sustainability of MediShield Life.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, this increase in premiums will particularly impact older Singaporeans, some of whom may not have accumulated sufficient MediSave funds over their working lifetime to cover these rising costs.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I am interested to know how effectively this support reaches those in need.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe this would be especially helpful for seniors whose MediSave balances may become depleted over time due to frequent hospitalisations and those who lack family support.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Ensuring accessibility to this support without additional administrative application burdens on the applicants' part, would help safeguard our seniors from the risk of being uninsured due to financial constraints or the lack of literacy to navigate application process.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe that financial incentives would be useful in empowering individuals to act according to their preference for a healthier lifestyle.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This approach not only encourages preventive action, but may also, over time, reduce the burden of claims on MediShield Life, ultimately helping to contain premium burden for everyone.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In this regard, I hope MOH can consider broadening the range of preventive actions that qualify for incentives, beyond physical activities alone.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, regular health screenings, vaccinations and active management of chronic conditions could also be rewarded, as they play a crucial role in detecting and addressing health issues early.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Additionally, could MOH consider offering a tiered discount system, where individuals, who consistently participate in preventive care initiatives or over multiple years might earn progressively larger discounts on their premiums?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Such measures would further encourage longer-term commitment to healthier living.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Under this model, individuals could receive additional subsidies if they demonstrate improved health outcomes over time, such as better control of blood pressure or blood sugar levels.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This would serve as an incentive for individuals to actively manage their conditions and could, in the long run, lead to reduced claims on MediShield Life by decreasing complications related to chronic diseases.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Today, as we are faced with the dual pressures of an ageing population and rising medical costs, the latest adjustments on policy claim limits and expansion of claimable items towards advanced therapeutics, as well as outpatient and home-based care, signal the Government's commitment towards supporting Singaporeans to care for their health and well-being.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As we continue to navigate those challenges, I believe that the healthcare needs of vulnerable groups, including our seniors and lower-income households, must be prioritised.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These groups would likely feel the impact of rising premiums most over the longer term, especially if they do not have enough MediSave funds.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Therefore, I hope that the Government can ensure that resources for these groups remain accessible and sufficient.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I also hope that the Government can use this as an opportunity to consider how incentives in MediShield Life premiums and claims can better support preventive measures, as we work towards more sustainable healthcare for future generations.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: It is especially relevant now, with a growing ageing population.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The amendments before the House align the MediShield Life Scheme with the evolving healthcare needs.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: By enabling better oversight through approvals and conditions for medical institutions, the Bill promotes service quality and cost-effective healthcare delivery.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: These updates enhance Singapore's ability to deliver sustainable healthcare coverage, while managing public health funds efficiently.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The Minister can impose conditions on service delivery modes like telemedicine, the provision of outpatient medical services remotely and at permanent premises to ensure appropriate healthcare delivery.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The ability to revoke or suspend approvals ensures compliance with the Healthcare Services Act 2020, promoting accountability and service quality.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The Bill also ensures only treatments provided by approved institutions under specified conditions will qualify for MediShield Life claims, ensuring proper allocation of insurance funds.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: In my view, some of these changes, while introducing new compliance requirements, will benefit medical institutions from more streamlined approval processes and clearer service delivery standards, and will lead to improve patient care.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: During this transition, in order to avoid any disruption in claims processing, close coordination between insurers and health providers will be required.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Second, will insured persons undergoing treatments, under the previous framework, continue to receive coverage during the transition period?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Third, will the conditions for service delivery vary across institutions and how will these be communicated to the public?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Fourth, what processes will be in place for institutions or individuals to appeal decisions related to approval revocations or for denial of claims?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: MediShield Life has become an indispensable pillar of Singapore's healthcare system, providing critical coverage that ensures no Singaporean is left without access to essential medical treatment.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This amendment Bill seeks to modernise and expand MediShield Life to meet the evolving healthcare needs.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I commend the Ministry for its proactive efforts, especially, given today's complex and dynamic healthcare landscape.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: However, with this expansion comes the responsibility to carefully manage costs, ensuring that the scheme remains sustainable and the premiums remain affordable for all insured persons.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In recent years, we have seen significant growth in the scope of medical services in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This includes expanding telemedicine and digital health services, which offer accessible options like remote consultations and monitoring.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Advanced treatments in areas like oncology and personalised medicine are also available, but often come at a high cost.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Additionally, the importance of mental health has become increasingly apparent and pertinent, and there is a growing need for affordable mental health services within our healthcare framework.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As the demands for these varied and sometimes high-cost services grow, we must consider how MediShield Life can responsibly support new healthcare needs, including mental health, while maintaining the scheme's financial sustainability.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Without careful oversight, a surge in claims could increase premiums for all insured members, affecting affordability.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: To address these challenges and safeguard MediShield Life's financial sustainability, I urge the Ministry to consider three key measures.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: By prioritising treatments that benefit the majority, we can ensure that resources are used effectively, preserving MediShield Life's affordability and accessibility.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Regular reviews of MediShield Life's financial performance, especially concerning new services and approved institutions, would enable us to make timely adjustments.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: These reviews could act as an early warning system, identifying areas where costs may rise unsustainably and allowing for targeted measures to keep premiums stable.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Thirdly, is to explore sustainable mental health coverage.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As the demand for mental health grows, I encourage the Ministry to consider ways to sustainably include essential mental health treatments in MediShield Life's coverage.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Addressing mental health needs is critical to holistic care.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: By exploring financial sustainability options, we can ensure MediShield Life continues to evolve with our society's needs.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Expanding coverage thoughtfully and sustainably will allow MediShield Life to remain a robust healthcare safety net that provides affordable, reliable and essential care to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: With this revision, MediShield Life will be able to approve medical institutions and services that are eligible for coverage under this scheme.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: With these measures, MediShield Life will continue to be an affordable, reliable and relevant healthcare safety net for all Singaporeans. : Mr Deputy Speaker, in conclusion, I support the Ministry's efforts to keep MediShield Life responsive to Singaporeans' healthcare needs.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: However, we must ensure that these amendments are implemented with financial prudence.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: By establishing clear coverage criteria, conducting regular financial reviews and exploring sustainable ways to include essential mental health services, we can safeguard MediShield Life's long-term viability.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Notwithstanding the concerns I raised earlier, I truly believe MediShield Life can continue to be a source of peace of mind for every Singaporean, supporting a healthier, more resilient society.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In the context of my comments on this Bill, I declare that I am a medical practitioner in private practice.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: And very importantly, this is regardless of age or pre-existing conditions.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It is a key pillar to enable access to good healthcare, along with the other tenets of the "S+3M" strategy outlined by the Minister of State earlier, the rest being subsidies, MediSave and MediFund.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Among other things, these would have to include ensuring quality of standards and to the extent possible, clinical guidelines to standardise care, regulations to ensure cost-effectiveness of treatment, transparency in billing and claims by the providers and accountability mechanisms, especially at the level of the providers.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: These come with a view to keep the MediShield Life claims within what is fair, what is reasonable and what is clinically appropriate, and so that claims are neither allowed to be excessive nor exorbitant for any particular condition.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The eventual intent, of course, is to ensure that at the national level, the MediShield Life premium remains affordable to sustain for every Singaporean.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I note that substantive portions of the amendment Bill look at two key areas: the first being approval, revocation or suspensions of medical institutions in respect of approved medical treatment or services under the new sections 3A and 3B; as well as amendments to Part 4 of the Act under Offences, specifically under False or Incorrect Health Declaration, Means Declaration or Claim Application.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: My view is that the amendments proposed are sound and reasonable.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It covers the breadth of licensable healthcare services and service delivery modes under the Healthcare Services Act in 2020 and lends further clarity to offences that could fall within the remit of MediShield Life claims.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: With the changes not only to MediShield Life but also with the ongoing implementation by MOH for Healthier SG initiatives, the upcoming Health Information Bill slated next year and recent announcements by the Ministry relating to information sharing across public and private sector institutions on the National Electronic Health Records, I urge the Ministry to engage private sector medical practitioners more closely on the last-mile impact and concerns arising from the impending broad shifts to the healthcare landscape.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Specifically, those coming from smaller or singular clinic entities and how they could be better supported in navigating these slew of changes that are ongoing and anticipated in the coming years.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I understand that perception surveys and stakeholder engagements are done from time to time to gauge the readiness of private healthcare providers on the potential changes that could be afoot in the healthcare sector.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The structure and relationship of private hospitals vis-a-vis the private medical practitioners, are more heterogeneous and not as singular and strongly rooted as those in the public hospitals and that could add further complexity to ground implementation of MediShield Life claims.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: For MediShield Life to be truly accessible and impactful to every Singaporean, as hoped and as intended by policy, a key enabler would be the medical practitioners themselves, who need to be supported well at the last mile in order to offer good custodianship of this scheme.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I hope the Ministry will lend emphasis and greater support for this group as the proposed changes to the MediShield Life take root in the coming year.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This also runs in parallel to the point made for patients at the last mile by the hon Member Ms Jessica Tan about considering MediShield Life changes in wider context and not in isolation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Nevertheless, I seek clarifications on four key areas to ensure fair healthcare access for all Singaporeans, especially the elderly and those with limited mobility.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I am concerned about the potential impact of moving towards online publication on our less digitally savvy seniors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While I understand the intention to leverage digital platforms, many seniors still struggle with digital literacy.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This shift could create a significant barrier to assessing vital information about their healthcare costs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Unexpected increases without sufficient warning could place an undue financial burden on vulnerable individuals.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Members have also raised questions on the changes to MediShield Life that were announced last month as part of the 2024 review.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As the Members have pointed out, this review of MediShield Life is a significant one.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: First, we will ensure MediShield Life coverage remains adequate for Singaporeans, given the rise in healthcare costs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are most concerned about major health episodes that result in large medical bills and cause financial strain.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Therefore, MediShield Life's claim limits will be increased to better protect Singaporeans against such bills.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Second, healthcare is increasingly delivered outside of the hospital, in the community and home settings.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is more convenient for patients and their family members.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To support this shift, we will enhance outpatient coverage significantly to include treatments, such as for depression.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Third, technological advancements have enabled the emergence of novel drugs such as cell, tissue and gene therapy products.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: While these have the potential to cure serious diseases, many of them are very expensive.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Insurance, like MediShield Life, is a suitable way to finance such treatments, which are costly but have a low incidence rate.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Therefore, MediShield Life's coverage will be extended to selected high-cost treatments that are clinically- and cost-effective.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For more than nine in 10 Singaporeans, the additional support will more than offset the premium increase over the next three years.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Members have raised comments in three broad areas: one, affordability of healthcare for patients; two, affordability of premiums for policyholders; and three, sustainability of the scheme.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling, Ms Jessica Tan and Dr Wan Rizal asked how the MediShield Life Council had selected the new areas that MediShield Life coverage would be extended to in this review and whether other areas such as pre- and post-hospitalisation treatments or mental health services were considered for coverage in the review.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In general, the Council prioritised treatments that had significant affordability gaps, were suitable for risk-pooling, clinically- and cost-effective and supported the shifting of care to lower-cost settings.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In making recommendations on where to enhance or extend coverage, the Council strikes a fine balance between improving patient affordability and premium impact.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: That is not to say that patients do not have support for their pre- and post-hospitalisation needs, such as consultations or scans, when seeking subsidised care at our public healthcare institutions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Patients can already access a combination of subsidies and MediSave, where applicable, for these.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling and Ms Jessica Tan also asked about the impact of the deductible changes on patients, especially the lower income.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The inpatient deductible has not been adjusted since the introduction of MediShield Life in 2015.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: With rising medical bills, the deductible has become less effective in sieving out smaller, more affordable bills that can be paid for by MediSave.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The revision in deductibles will refocus MediShield Life's coverage on larger medical bills which, in turn, will moderate the premium impact.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: With significant enhancements to outpatient coverage and home-based medical care, we will also introduce a new outpatient deductible of $500.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This will keep the scheme focused on larger outpatient bills and ensure premiums remain sustainable.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Government will raise MediSave withdrawal limits in tandem with the MediShield Life changes to help patients pay for the higher deductibles.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I understand the Members' concern about the lower-income households and seniors who may not have sufficient MediSave.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The MediSave top-ups by the Government will provide some help for these more vulnerable groups.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I also wish to assure the House that Singaporeans who face difficulty affording their bills after subsidies, MediSave and MediShield Life, can apply for financial assistance such as MediFund.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: No one will be denied access to appropriate healthcare due to an inability to pay.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked how vulnerable groups, such as the lower-income, elderly and those with chronic conditions, will be supported in affording their premiums.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I wish to assure the Members that we have taken special care to support them.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As announced by the Government earlier, premium increases will be capped at 35%, which mostly benefits older age groups.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Premium increases will also be phased in evenly over the next three years to help all policyholders.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On top of this, older Singaporeans in lower- to middle-income households will also benefit from the means-tested premium subsidy enhancements that were recently announced.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: They will receive higher means-tested premium subsidies of up to 60%, from up to 50% today.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In addition, the MediShield Life premiums of older Pioneer Generation seniors will continue to be fully covered.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng, Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Gerald Giam also asked how lower-income individuals who are living in or owning properties with high AV will be supported.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is true that such individuals receive lower means-tested premium subsidies on account of their higher AV properties.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is because those who live in properties with a higher AV would generally be better off than those who live in properties with a lower AV.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: While this approach is not perfect, it strikes a balance between being more precise in assessing applicants' means, while keeping the process simpler for most applicants.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: However, the Government periodically reviews the eligibility criteria for subsidies so that Singaporeans with greater needs can continue to receive the support they require.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For instance, the AV thresholds were recently raised earlier this year.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: With this, those staying in or owning these lower-value private properties can still qualify for premium subsidies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Those who need more help or are facing extenuating circumstances may appeal for more assistance, which would be assessed on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling and Dr Wan Rizal have commented about rising healthcare costs and the impact to the long-term sustainability of the MediShield Life scheme, especially with the expansions of MediShield Life coverage.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is indeed an area that the Government is committed to addressing.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have implemented various strategies on this front.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: First, we have been re-designing the healthcare system to better support right-siting of care from our acute hospitals to other settings such as the outpatient, community and home settings where one can receive the same care at lower costs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Our enhancements to MediShield Life coverage through the recent review will also support patients in accessing care at such settings.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Second, we have been applying Health Technology Assessments to more high-cost technologies and drugs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This allows us to rigorously assess that a new treatment is clinically- and cost-effective before we extend financing coverage to it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This also allows the Government to negotiate for more competitive prices from industry, moderating the cost impact to our system.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Third, and most important, is our increased focus on staying healthy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is why we have Healthier SG, which is our national initiative focusing on preventive health and chronic disease management.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have introduced premium discounts in this review, to complement our national efforts to incentivise healthier living, where Healthpoints can be redeemed for MediShield Life premium discounts.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I am glad that Ms Ng Ling Ling is supportive of this idea, and has raised useful suggestions such as broadening the range of activities that qualify for incentives and implementing a system to encourage sustained activity.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We will take all of these into account as we study the outcomes of this pilot, before deciding whether to make the scheme permanent.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These will go some way in providing relief for Singaporeans amidst rising healthcare costs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Government will continue to work with the MediShield Life Council to review the scheme regularly to ensure that it remains a source of assurance for large healthcare bills and that its premiums remain affordable for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: At the same time, we will continue to press on with our efforts to keep our healthcare system sustainable for many years to come.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I will now move on to address Members' questions and comments on the MediShield Life Scheme (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: First, on supporting the expansion of coverage to models of care received outside the physical premises of providers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As mentioned earlier, we will enhance MediShield Life to cover more types of care, such as home-based medical or telehealth services delivered outside of the traditional hospital setting.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This will allow more patients to receive the care that they need in a more convenient way.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Going forward, we expect to see the emergence of more care models where treatment or services are completely delivered outside of a physical medical institution.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These care models may eventually become the standard of care.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To Mr Yip Hon Weng's query on how patients can know which services are claimable under MediShield Life, I would like to share that new approved medical treatment or services, including home care and telehealth services, will be publicised through the MediShield Life Council's report, on the MediShield Life website and be stated clearly in the MediShield Life Scheme Regulations 2015.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In addition, the expansion of the scheme's coverage will be complemented by amendments setting out the framework for approvals and suspensions and revocations of approvals, of medical institutions under the scheme.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Gerald Giam spoke about the criteria for approval of medical institutions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This framework will allow MOH to continue safeguarding and ensuring the appropriate use of MediShield Life monies, while maintaining a clear and robust framework for managing medical institutions participating under the scheme.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For instance, to be approved, the medical institution will need to have a valid licence issued under the Healthcare Services Act 2020.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The scope of the medical institution's approval under the scheme is also tied to the specific licensable healthcare services that it is authorised to provide by its licence, as well as their respective service delivery modes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The key appointment holders of the medical institution, as well as any medical practitioner that is employed or engaged to provide the approved medical treatment or services in that medical institution must also not be found to be in breach of certain requirements, such as being convicted of an offence involving fraud or dishonesty.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Minister for Health may also impose conditions of approval, which could include requiring the medical institution to ensure that MediShield Life claims are submitted in accordance with the relevant claim rules.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng raised concerns about the broad powers for approvals, suspensions and revocations, and how they will affect patients currently receiving treatment and services.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Similarly, Mr Neil Parekh asked how the conditions of approval would apply and be communicated, whether there would be continuity of coverage for insured persons under the new framework, as well as the processes in place for the approval or rejection of applications, or for appeals related to revocations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: First, as stated in my opening speech, the Minister is empowered to grant approvals to medical institutions under the new amendments.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Second, enforcement measures can now also be tailored to respond to specific medical institutions, or specific treatments or services offered by them that fail to comply with the requirements or their conditions of approval under the MediShield Life Act.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: With this, when we take action against the medical institution for other treatment or services which are not provided in compliance with the Act, we can still safeguard the patient's ability to continue making claims for approved medical treatments or services that are provided in compliance with the Act.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: A single medical institution today may be delivering multiple care models or treatment through different licensed healthcare services or different service delivery modes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Today, enforcement measures taken against an approved medical institution in a non-compliant area would involve suspending or revoking the approval of the entire medical institution.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This could be when a non-compliant service delivery mode is used by the medical institution.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The approval for the medical institution to submit claims for other treatments or services via other delivery modes remain valid, and patients can still be covered by MediShield Life.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if there would be transitional arrangements in situations where approvals to medical institutions are suspended or revoked, to avoid disruptions to ongoing care of patients.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The amendments require medical institutions providing any non-compliant medical treatment or services to inform all patients of the suspension or revocation of approval of such medical treatment or services immediately.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Minister for Health can also permit claims for such treatment or services provided during the suspension or after the revocation, if necessary, to safeguard the patient's interest.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This power to safeguard MediShield Life monies will be exercised judiciously, to minimise any undue care disruptions to patients.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Third, let me assure Members of the House that there are safeguards in place to ensure accountability and due process.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For these reasons, we do not think it is ideal to include statutory consultation requirements before restricting service delivery modes, as Mr Yip Hon Weng has suggested.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In cases where patient safety is at risk or where the provider has committed fraud, restrictions of coverage will likely need to be immediate.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: That said, any restriction of service delivery modes will be exercised judiciously and only applied where the conditions of approval have been breached.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In addition, in suspending or revoking an approval, the medical institution concerned must be given written notice and a reasonable opportunity to make representations as to why the approval should not be suspended or revoked, which is already our practice today.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Dr Syed Harun also asked that we engage private medical practitioners to support them in navigating these changes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Indeed, private providers are an important part of our healthcare ecosystem.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We will continue to partner and educate them on these changes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Altogether, the amendments in this category allow MediShield Life to be more flexible and responsive to the evolving healthcare landscape.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Act also needs to be amended to better support premium recovery.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For a universal scheme like MediShield Life, premium recovery is necessary to discourage policyholders who can afford to, but wilfully decide not to fulfil their premium obligations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Without a robust set of premium recovery measures, it is entirely possible that premium defaults could go up, translating to bad debts which could materially impact the Fund and result in higher premiums for all.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This would be unfair to policyholders who have paid their premiums and undermines collective responsibility.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This means that the vast majority of the policyholders are able to pay their premiums.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is made possible through a comprehensive support system to help Singaporeans, especially those of less means, with their premiums, thereby reducing the likelihood of individuals defaulting in the first place.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I had covered these in detail earlier in my speech.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Even with these support measures, there will be a small group of individuals who do not fulfil their premium obligations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: When deduction of the premium from the policyholder's or his designated payor's MediSave fails, the Government embarks on a series of premium recovery measures.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Family members, such as parents and spouses, will be identified to pay for their loved ones' premiums using MediSave, on an opt-out basis.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Those notified may choose to cancel this payment arrangement if they do not wish to help with their family members' premiums.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Eligible individuals will also be invited to apply for APS.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: MOH works with the Ministry of Social and Family Development to conduct proactive outreach to low-income, elderly individuals who may need help with their APS applications.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Quarterly reminder letters are also sent to remind policyholders to top up their MediSave accounts, change the premium payor or arrange for monthly instalment payment plan for their owed premiums.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Significant efforts are made to ensure that those who are genuinely in need receive support to pay their premiums.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Only when these efforts are exhausted, would premium enforcement commence.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Before any enforcement action can be taken against defaulters, a demand note must first be served.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: A demand note notifies defaulters of their outstanding premiums and gives them sufficient time to pay their premiums, before interest and penalties are imposed and further enforcement measures like agent appointments are taken.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These measures take reference from income tax recovery measures and are already provided for in the existing legislation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: IRAS, which is a prescribed recovery body under the MediShield Life scheme, sends the demand notes via mail, as provided for under the legislation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: However, there are some defaulters who are difficult to reach via post.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This includes individuals who do not update their residential or correspondence addresses with the Government after they renounce their Singapore Citizenship or lose their Permanent Residency status, as well as individuals residing overseas in areas with unreliable postage services.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As demand notes are often not successfully delivered to such individuals, enforcement against this group is limited in effectiveness.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Therefore, the Act amendments provide for more avenues through which demand notes may be served, including via digital means.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, to address Mr Gerald Giam's concern, this is actually on top of existing means such as the physical mail.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This could include IRAS' "myTax Portal" and CPF Board's "my cpf" portal.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We will work with both agencies to explore the feasibility of tapping on their electronic service platforms.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is a fair approach – Singaporeans already use these portals to manage their tax- and CPF-related matters, and it is reasonable for the Government to make contact with them through such channels.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
