text: We will explore with IRAS and CPF Board on the feasibility of sending notifications through SMSes and emails, to ensure demand notes are brought to the attention of the recipients.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As I mentioned earlier, everyone must pay for their premiums as part of our collective responsibility to one another and to ensure the sustainability of the scheme.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is why we have a strong set of recovery and enforcement actions in place.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: However, we are mindful that some Singaporeans may face difficulties paying for their premiums due to complex circumstances.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Hence, we adopt a compassionate stance towards premium recovery and enforcement.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This way, we do not inadvertently cause hardship to those who are unable to meet their premium obligations.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For example, we withhold enforcement from vulnerable groups as such elderly above the age of 85 years old.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: One proxy for an individual's ability to pay their premiums is their means information.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The proposed amendment will support the use of means information to enable a calibration of our premium recovery and enforcement efforts when it comes to Singaporeans with genuine difficulty in affording their premiums.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about how such means information would be used, the criteria used to calibrate enforcement efforts and whether such criteria would reduce accessibility for individuals that do not meet the bar.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Gerald Giam also raised concern that some Singaporeans with complex circumstances may face difficulties paying premiums and this is precisely why we are creating this avenue to allow for a more calibrated approach.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: On the contrary, it is meant to help Singaporeans – by ensuring that premium enforcement measures are targeted at those who have more means, while calibrating enforcement measures for those who have less means.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Means information is used to derive per capita household income.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is aligned to many other Government schemes that differentiate subsidies based on PCHI to ensure that resources are targeted at those who need more support.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We acknowledge the Members' concern that this may not differentiate retired seniors with different financial situations, including those who are asset-rich and cash-poor.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is why we have APS, which serves as a discretionary safety net, to give support to those who may have fallen through the cracks and face genuine difficulty affording their premiums.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Eligibility for APS is assessed holistically with appeals considered on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration the unique social and financial circumstances, and needs of individuals.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For individuals who do not qualify for APS, we will still exercise flexibility for those with extenuating circumstances, on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For instance, we may delay premium enforcement until their financial circumstances improve.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: If some require a longer time to pay their premiums, they may contact the CPF Board, which oversees premium collection, to work out an instalment payment plan.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For premium enforcement, we work with the MediShield Life Council on detailed criteria as well as the appeal guidelines for cases at the margins, to ensure enforcement does not unfairly penalise such groups.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Besides refining provisions to support premium recovery efforts, we are also making some amendments to clarify and strengthen existing administrative processes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the potential impact of such a move on our less digitally savvy seniors.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These will continue to be delivered through mail, SMS or email, depending on the policyholder's contact information available to the CPF Board.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, Singaporeans, including seniors, already have many platforms through which to access information about premiums, and this amendment will not change this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Instead, this amendment is simply intended to allow MediShield Life premiums to be published on a website instead of through legislation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In enabling this, we will significantly streamline the administration of the scheme.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is also the approach already in place for other healthcare schemes such as CareShield Life, for which premiums are available online instead of through legislation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Mr Gerald Giam spoke about the stability and predictability of premium rates.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The premiums are already published on the website today and we have also given advance notice for the next policy cycle – it is actually three years' worth of premiums in the press release and also in the Council's report.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: To address also another administrative point that Mr Gerald Giam raised on individuals who unknowingly provide false or misleading information – actually, such conduct does not amount to an offence under the Act.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Such efforts allow us to reach more citizens, including seniors, and ensures that no one is left behind.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Are there any clarifications for Minister of State?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: First, the Minister of State assured us earlier that no one would lose MediShield Life coverage due to an inability to pay premiums.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: How about policyholders who miss payments for reasons such as ineligibility for premium support despite appeals, missed reminders or other issues.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Are there any circumstances under which they could lose MediShield Life coverage due to a failure to pay premiums?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I know the Minister of State provided a list of conditions in her response just now, but it is not clear if it potentially includes TCM.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In respect of the second question – first, I just want to add that the MediShield Life scheme is something that we review and its coverage is something that we will continue to monitor and assess.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, this is something that will allow for us to continue to look at it and if it meets the criteria, it would be something that can be included.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is something that we will look at on a regular basis.
